title: precon-v2 recorded answer
description: The executor's one recorded answer for a precon-v2 run (references/precon-v2-contract.md section 5), handed to `record-answer`. Closed at every level. This schema holds the SHAPE only: every content rule (a decided line with no source, an assumed line with no why, a parked line without one of the three reasons, a quietly resolved line, a needs-research question resolved, a missing or blank gate line) is a refusal of record-answer, exit 5 with the rule named, so fields those rules read are optional here.

run_id.description: this run's id; equal to the input's run_id

session_id.description: the executor's session, the adapter's answer_fields.session_id; equal to the input's invocation.session_id

why.description: the one-line reason for the tier, as said aloud

no_scope_doc.description: napkin only: the owner took 'no scope doc, straight to /blueprint'; the run then carries no line and writes no file

doc.description: a NEW doc only: its title (the <Idea> of the title line) and its Intent line

questions.description: every question put to the owner in this run

touches.description: the ledger line ids the question touches

answer.description: the owner's answer, verbatim; absent or blank when unanswered

needs_research.description: the question needs outside research: it is parked as needs research and never resolved in the run

lines.description: every line the executor asserts: new Decisions lines, lines settled, lines passed forward, and open calls

trace.description: where the line comes from. `ledger`: a ledger line id of the scope doc this run read (the line passed forward, or settled); `question`: the id of a question of this run the owner answered; `owner_words`: the owner's words, quoted; `repo_path`: a path in the workspace; `assumed`: the executor's why (assumed lines only). Checked by station_core/answer.py and precon's own rules, never by this schema alone.

row.description: the id of the ledger row this line decides, settles, passes forward or moves (the row's id is the trace: the line is judged by it and its words are never matched against that row). Absent on a NEW line, one that names no existing row. A line whose trace is `ledger` names its row by that trace; `row` may repeat it and may not differ from it.

reason.description: a parked line: needs research, needs prototype, or waiting on <x>

waits_on.description: an open line: the owner's call it waits on

out_of_scope.description: what the owner ruled out, each with its reason and its trace

trace.description: where the line comes from. `ledger`: a ledger line id of the scope doc this run read (the line passed forward, or settled); `question`: the id of a question of this run the owner answered; `owner_words`: the owner's words, quoted; `repo_path`: a path in the workspace; `assumed`: the executor's why (assumed lines only). Checked by station_core/answer.py and precon's own rules, never by this schema alone.

research.description: paths or links to research the owner did himself

open_items.description: unresolved threads for the next sitting, written under Open:

exit_test.description: the cold read. In the run that built requests: `rows`, the rows named (their results are read from readers' sidecars). In a later run: `cold_read_doc`, `summary` and `dispositions`.

sitting.description: `ends` on the sitting's last run (the read-back and the full stop); `continues` on a round that hands on to the next

gate.description: the one-line justification that every branch was visited or parked (on a round that continues: what this run visited and what it leaves open). Required by record-answer's rule gate-missing, not by this schema
